title: 5 Open-Source AI Models That Are Catching Claude Fast
description:
Everyone is talking about Claude Fable 5.
Almost nobody is talking about the open-source models catching up.
If you're a developer, AI builder, or founder, these are five models worth keeping on your radar.

GLM-5.2 is the first open-weight model to outperform Claude Fable 5 on Design Arena's coding leaderboard. And it's MIT licensed.

DeepSeek V4 Pro brings a massive 1 million token context window, strong coding performance, and one of the lowest costs among frontier AI models.

Kimi K2.7-Code is built for AI agents, offers stronger MCP support, and reduces token usage compared to previous versions.

Qwen 3.5 supports more than 200 languages, runs locally, and delivers coding performance surprisingly close to leading closed-source models.

MiniMax M3 combines a 1 million token context window, multimodal capabilities, and frontier-level coding performance in a single open-weight model.

The biggest shift isn't that open-source AI exists.
It's that developers no longer have to choose between performance and openness.

A year ago, the best AI models were almost entirely closed-source.
Today, that gap is shrinking faster than most people expected.
Save this list before your next AI project.
